answer.why: Only an insider would know that phrase: it is the wording on the letter when you are confirmed in an appointment and made substantive in the grade, and I laughed out loud at it. It signals the developer actually knows the service. Minister Salary is the headline everyone in Singapore has an opinion about, so it feels like clickbait, and I have sat through enough of that debate at work.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical, slightly cheeky game about the pay-benchmark debate, probably a clicker or a scandal sim where you chase the top salary and make jokes about 'ministers are paid too much'. I would expect it to be shallow and to get details wrong, but it would get the most clicks. It might also feel a bit political, and I would be wary of it.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, insider-flavoured career sim about the slow grind of promotions, probationary periods, appraisals and getting your grade confirmed. I would expect bureaucratic humour, waiting for results, and a quiet sense of accuracy. It is not catchy to outsiders, and it is a clunky name, but it is the one that makes me think the writers have actually sat through an appraisal cycle.

  [PAY] Annual package: $2,363,240, including a National Bonus of 3 months
  [APPRAISAL] Your performance is described as "outstanding, with clear potential for wider responsibility".

THIS YEAR: Polling Day, Again
Parliament is dissolved on a Tuesday. Nobody is surprised; the tents went up in the void decks a fortnight ago. Your face is larger on the poster this time, which means the swing is, in some small part, about you.

  A) Campaign on the record.
  B) Walk every block, every night, for nine days.

agent.why: Walking every block worked last time and I trust it more than a record that is about to be argued over, especially with STAND falling.
agent.confused_by: STAND dropping 14 after a year where I asked a reasonable question; unclear what the game is penalising.
agent.note: The line about a face being larger on the poster meaning the swing is about you is a nice insider touch. Still odd to be DPM and still described for 'wider responsibility' at 62.
agent.remember: Y37 (age 62): GE again, STAND 54 (-14). Chose B, walked every block for nine days as in Y32. Watch GE margin, whether STAND recovers, and the fallout from my Cabinet question about indicator-based pay.

best_moment.what: Answering the third point of the wrong post publicly, then having it come back in Y35 as the scheme amended and credited to the post's author. Small, bureaucratic, very believable.

worst_moment.what: The final GE: walking every block for nine days again, same choice as Y32, with STAND already falling. It felt like a repeat and the ending arrived without a real payoff.

skip_year.why: The Cabinet question about ministers being paid on indicators they set raised the game's own theme, but nothing visible came of it. STAND just fell and I never saw the backlash or the benchmark review.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y3 nominated the quiet officer who does real work
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: She became Deputy Secretary and put my name in at Y15

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y33 answered the third point of the wrong post publicly
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Y35 the Third Point returned and the scheme was amended as the post suggested

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y39 declassified: let the officer decide without hearing from me
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending card says that choice raised my ceiling to DPM, and the legacy line says two people stayed because of me

answer.held_back_by: Nothing really. I went from MP to PM far too quickly, and the file says no ceiling. If anything held me back it was STAND sliding in my last years, from my own pushing on pay and workload questions.
answer.ending_fair_why: PM, clean file and a legacy of people who stayed is what a careful, boring career deserves. The pay line, twice the entry-grade minister's salary, is a nice dry touch. I'd have liked the Y36 question to matter in the ending.
answer.chase_next: Stay in the service and never enter politics, just to see how high a permanent secretary track goes and whether the game models the grades properly. The declassified ceiling line makes me curious about a lower-ceiling life.
answer.play_again_why: The loose threads, the contractor cousin, the board offer and the leaker, never resolved, so I want to see whether a different path pays them off. It's short enough on the MRT.

tone_breaks.line: Y39 declassified: 'Most people's files do.' / 'Nobody told you that either.'
tone_breaks.note: The ceiling and party estimate reveal is a gentle wink at the system. It works as a reveal, but real files are not read out like this.

tone_breaks.line: Promotions: MP Y13, Parl Sec Y14, SPS Y18, Minister Y25
tone_breaks.note: Pace is unrealistic, and grade order was odd earlier. A Parl Sec title and SPS do not sit like that for a politician fresh from the service.
Mixing a DPM title with an MR1 grade at a ministry looked off to me. It reads as a mislabel.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is more about being confirmed, trusted and tested on small choices than about pay, though the pay line closes it neatly.
